texts.text: ENGLISH FOR DAILY LIFE
A2 · Volume 1 · Everyday Life
English for Daily Life takes an adult beginner who already knows a little English and
gives them the present and the past: what is, what they do, and what happened. Three
units follow six people who live at one address, so the vocabulary comes back week
after week instead of arriving once and leaving. Every unit has the same ten parts,
the same twelve kinds of exercise and the same support: a worked example at the top
of almost every task, a model before every piece of writing, a word bank under every
gap-fill and a checklist before you hand anything in. The Core track is for
everybody. The Plus track at the back of each unit is there when you are ready for
it, and optional when you are not. Answers for every closed question are in the book.
In this book
People and Routines
present simple
Home and Neighbourhood
there is/are
A Day in the City
present continuous vs present simple
By the end you will be able to
I can name the people around me: neighbour, flatmate, colleague.
I can use the present simple for routines and the present continuous for now.
I can understand a short conversation between neighbours.
I can describe a person’s day in 50–70 words.
I can name the rooms and parts of a building.
I can use there is and there are, and some, any, much and many.
CEFR A2 · Student Book with answer key · British English
